summary: Paul Horsch worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Paris and studied at Fribourg, Cambridge, Lausanne, and Marburg under Régamey, Renou, and Nobel, later teaching at Visva-Bharati (1952–1956) and Zurich (1959; 1967–1971).

Paul J. Griffiths is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Oxford and Wisconsin-Madison (PhD) under Gombrich, Kiyota, Sopa, and Hakamaya. He held posts at Notre Dame, UIC (2000–2007), and Duke University (~2008–2017).
Paul K. Nietupski specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University and held an academic post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

Paul Kingsbury is an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. His career includes posts at the Mayo Clinic (2016–2019), University of Southern California (2020–2022), and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (2022).
Paul Kiparsky is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at King Edward's School and at MIT under Morris Halle (~1962–1965), later holding a post at Stanford University (~1984).

Paul Kretschmer worked in linguistics, completing his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1889) under Johannes Schmidt and Hermann Diels. After posts in Berlin (1891) and Marburg (1897–1899), he served as professor at the University of Vienna (1899–1936).

Paul L. Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held a professorship at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).
Paul Marriot Wynch was an Indology scholar who attended the East India Company College (1809–1810) and served in the Bengal Civil Service from 1808.

Paul Masson-Oursel worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Foucher, Lévi, Bergson, Durkheim, Mauss, and Chavannes (~1903–1908). He spent his academic career at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919; Directeur d’études 1927–1953).

Paul McBain specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Chicago (2013–2015) and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (2018–2021), then took up a lectureship at Thammasat University in 2021.

Paul Mendes-Flohr worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University, subsequently serving as a director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and professor at the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Michael Toomey worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Bowdoin College and completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1975–1984), later teaching at Cornell University (~1983–1986).

Paul Mus was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate at Paris, studying under Lévi, Mauss, and Pelliot. He held posts at EFEO (1927–1940), Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale (1950).
Paul Olaf Bodding was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Oslo (1883–1889). He served as head of The Santal Mission of the Northern Churches from 1910 to 1933.

Paul Oltramare was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Geneva, Basel, and Paris under Paul Deussen and Michel Bréal. He taught at Collège Calvin (1876–1895) and the University of Geneva (1880–1881; professor 1893–1927).
Paul Passy worked in linguistics, having studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1881–1886). He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ~1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot was a scholar of Sinology, Central Asian studies, and Tibetology who studied under Chavannes, Lévi, and Senart. He held posts at EFEO (1900) and Collège de France (1909; 1911–1945), and edited T'oung Pao (1920–1945).

Paul R. Brass was an Indology scholar who studied at Harvard College, the University of Chicago, and Harvard University (~1960–1964). He spent his career at the University of Washington (~1967–2002), where he became Professor Emeritus.

Paul Regnaud specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Bergaigne and Hauvette-Besnault, completing degrees at EPHE and the University of Paris (PhD), and held the Sanskrit chair at the University of Lyon from 1887 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at Rennes and Paris. He held major posts at Strasbourg (1948–1956), Paris Nanterre (1964–1970), Université catholique de Louvain (~1970–1973), and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).
